case.note: A patient taking amantadine for influenza noticed her Parkinson's symptoms improve (Schwab 1969): a patient observation, not a label side effect. 1969 is the year of the first report; the US approval for parkinsonism came later.
Eyelash growth with glaucoma eye drops; approved in the US for sparse eyelashes in 2008.
An antidepressant whose sedation was known; low-dose doxepin was approved in the US for insomnia in 2010 (Krystal 2010). Added after the pharmacologist pass, before the next run.

Studied for male-pattern hair loss from its mechanism (5-alpha-reductase); approved in the US in 1997 (Kaufman 1998). Not expected from a side effect. Added after the pharmacologist pass, before the next run.

An anticholinergic whose reduced sweating was known; a topical form was approved in the US for axillary hyperhidrosis in 2018 (Glaser 2019). openFDA is queried with the US name glycopyrrolate. Added after the pharmacologist pass, before the next run.
Weight loss with liraglutide in diabetes; approved for weight management in 2014. OnSIDES v3.1.1 has no US label of liraglutide (two EU labels only).
Hair growth was seen with oral minoxidil for hypertension; topical minoxidil was approved for hair loss in 1988.
Weight loss with semaglutide in diabetes; approved for weight management in 2021 (Wilding 2021). Added after the pharmacologist pass, before the next run.

Developed for angina; erections were reported in trials; approved for erectile dysfunction in 1998. The US labels left in the primary run are pulmonary arterial hypertension labels written after the erectile effect was known, so the primary run is not clean for this case.
Studied for pulmonary arterial hypertension from its mechanism; approved in 2005. Not reachable from a side effect.

Given as a sedative to leprosy patients, whose lepra reactions improved (Sheskin 1965): a patient observation, not a label side effect. 1965 is the year of the first report; the US approval for this use came in 1998.
Tried in myeloma from the anti-angiogenesis hypothesis (Singhal 1999). Not reachable from a side effect. 1999 is the year of the first report; the US approval (with dexamethasone) came in 2006.
Weight loss with topiramate in epilepsy; studied for obesity (Bray 2003); approved in 2012 only in combination with phentermine.
